bull.t: Truck leadership and North America margins
bull.b: GM’s leading full-size pickup position supports a favorable mix and provides a durable earnings base in North America. The recovery of regional margins into the company’s target range, alongside sustained truck share leadership, strengthens operating resilience and supports future product launches.

The expansion of OnStar and Super Cruise adds higher-margin, recurring software and services revenue to GM’s vehicle business. A growing installed base, rising deferred revenue, and increased adoption can improve customer retention and make the revenue mix more durable over time.

Positive operating cash generation and higher free cash flow guidance provide GM with internal funding for product, software, and manufacturing investments. This financial capacity also supports debt service and shareholder returns while giving management flexibility through the vehicle cycle.

bear.b: Weak current profitability reduces the earnings buffer available to absorb cyclical pressure, while leverage near two times equity limits financial flexibility. Lower returns on equity also indicate that GM is converting its substantial asset base into earnings less efficiently than in earlier periods.

Elevated materials, logistics, semiconductor, and tariff costs can pressure vehicle margins across multiple quarters rather than acting as a single temporary expense. If these costs persist, GM may need pricing, productivity gains, or product-mix benefits to preserve its earnings trajectory.

bear.t: EV losses and restructuring cash charges
bear.b: GM’s EV transition remains financially burdensome because weaker volumes and capacity rightsizing require substantial restructuring cash outlays. Although management expects losses to improve, the continuing charges consume capital and highlight execution risk in building a profitable electrified portfolio.
